summary.en: Ottoman forces landed on Chios in response to a rising encouraged from Samos, and destroyed the island's population by killing, enslavement and flight. The scale of it turned European opinion toward the Greek cause, most visibly through Delacroix's painting of 1824.

body_html.en:
Chios was a wealthy island whose notables had wanted no part in the revolution. A small force from Samos landed in March 1822 and forced the issue; the Ottoman fleet arrived in April with orders to make an example of the island.

Over the following weeks tens of thousands were killed or sold into slavery and most of the survivors fled. The island did not recover for a century. In Europe the massacre did more than any Greek victory to make the war a popular cause, and Delacroix's Scenes from the Massacres of Chios, shown at the Paris Salon of 1824, fixed the image.
